blocks.text: *Effective:* 30 October 2026
*Data controller:* the Vidlun developer, support@vidlun.app
*Contact:* support@vidlun.app

bullets: *Audio never leaves your phone.* Speech recognition runs entirely on the device, with a model built into the app.

Only the *text* of a transcript leaves — to Anthropic's Claude language model (USA), to name the emotions, mood and topics of an entry and once a month to write a piece about your month. *Only if you agree to it.* Without your consent, Vidlun works as a plain journal.
Also what you write to us in the feedback form — but only when you tap "Send".
*No accounts, no sign-up, no analytics, no trackers, no advertising.* We do not sell any data.
Your entries are not stored on our servers. The text for analysis only passes through our proxy: we neither store it nor read it.

blocks.heading: 1. What is kept on your phone

rows: thirteen months, then deleted automatically; immediately if "Keep recordings" is off
Transcript, emotions, mood, topics, the difficult-state flag, time
Revision log: what the app proposed and what was changed
The saved monthly piece (and weekly ones from earlier versions)
Your consent to analysis: when it was given or withdrawn

blocks.text: None of this is sent to us. Deleting the app destroys all of it.

blocks.sub: 2.1 The text of an entry, for analysis by a language model

blocks.text: *What exactly.* The cleaned transcript of one entry. For the monthly piece: the date, the mood number, emotion codes, topics and the transcripts of a month's entries together.
*Where to.* Through our Cloudflare Workers proxy to Anthropic PBC (USA), to the API of the Claude language model.
*Why.*

bullets: To propose names for the emotions, the mood and the topics of an entry.

To notice whether an entry sounds like a very difficult state or thoughts of self-harm. The flag stays on the phone: after a very difficult entry, Vidlun offers a one-minute grounding exercise. It is not a diagnosis or a professional risk assessment.
To write a piece about your month once a month (with a subscription).

blocks.text: *This is sensitive data.* What you say about your feelings and how you are is data about mental health. The GDPR and Ukraine's Law on Personal Data Protection treat it as a special category, so it leaves the phone only with your explicit consent.

*Lawful basis.* Your explicit consent: GDPR (and UK GDPR) Art. 6(1)(a) and Art. 9(2)(a); Articles 7 and 11 of Ukraine's Law on Personal Data Protection. You give it on a separate screen before your first entry, or once after the update if Vidlun is already on your phone.
*How to withdraw it.* Turn off "Entry analysis" in Me. From then on no text leaves the phone, and entries already saved stay as they are. Withdrawing does not make the processing before it unlawful.

*Without consent* you can record, see the transcript, name emotions and the mood yourself, keep the journal and do the grounding exercise. The emotion names Vidlun heard in an entry, the topics and the monthly piece will not be there.

*The proxy stores no content.* It has no database of entries and keeps no log of request content. It exists for one reason: to hold the language model's API key outside the app, because a key shipped inside an app can be read by anyone.

*Anthropic* processes the text as our processor, under our contract with it: it is not used to train models, and is retained for a limited period for abuse prevention. See https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms and https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy.
*What Anthropic never receives:* audio, your name, email, contacts, location, advertising identifiers, device or install identifiers.

blocks.sub: 2.2 Checking that a request comes from Vidlun

blocks.text: *What exactly.* So that our proxy does not become free access to the language model for anyone, the app proves it is genuine with Apple App Attest. A key is created in the phone's secure chip, and Apple confirms it belongs to Vidlun on a real iPhone. The proxy keeps a random identifier for that key, its public part and a usage counter.
*What is not there:* your name, Apple ID, email or anything from your entries. We cannot tell who you are from the key's identifier.
*Why.* To let only the genuine app reach the proxy, and to limit how often one phone can call it.
*Where to.* The key's identifier and public part are kept in Cloudflare's storage; the confirmation comes from Apple.
*How long.* The record of a key deletes itself after 180 days without any request from that phone; every request extends it.
*Lawful basis* (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f), Article 11 of Ukraine's Law on Personal Data Protection): our legitimate interest in protecting the service from abuse.

Handled by Apple and RevenueCat, Inc. (USA). They receive an anonymous install identifier, the Apple receipt, purchase and renewal events, the store country and the device type. *No entry content reaches them.*
Lawful basis: performance of our contract with you. See https://www.revenuecat.com/privacy.
Cloudflare, as the network intermediary, sees the address a request came from. It is used only to rate-limit requests and is not stored alongside anything of yours.
*What exactly.* Only what you type into the "Write to us" form in your profile, plus the app version and the iOS version — the first thing support asks.
*Where to.* Through the same Cloudflare Workers proxy, as an email to our support mailbox. Cloudflare delivers the email; the mailbox is hosted by Google (Gmail).
*Why.* So we can read it and, where needed, reply. It happens only when you tap "Send"; the app never writes on its own.
*Lawful basis* (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f), Article 11 of Ukraine's Law on Personal Data Protection): our legitimate interest in answering the messages we are sent.

*How long.* On the phone, only until the email has gone (with no connection the note waits in the app and goes at the next launch). The proxy stores nothing. The email stays in the support mailbox while we deal with it and is deleted no later than a year after it arrived.

*What is never sent:* entries, transcripts, audio, feelings, mood — nothing from the journal. The form does not know who you are: the email carries no name, no email address and no device identifier. If you leave your address in the text, we use it only to reply.

bullets: *Microphone* — to record. Without it, Vidlun is a text journal.
*Notifications* — only for the reminder you switch on and set in your profile. The phone schedules it itself; there is no push server, and nobody outside can send you a notification through Vidlun.

blocks.text: If you have iCloud Backup on, the app's data — entries and audio — is included in your device backup. That happens on Apple's side under Apple's policy, not ours. You can turn it off for this app in iOS settings.
The Backup and Readable export files from your profile are not encrypted: they hold your whole journal. Keep them where nobody else can read them.

Under the GDPR and the UK GDPR you have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability, to withdraw consent, and to complain to a supervisory authority. Ukraine's Law on Personal Data Protection (Article 8) gives you the right to know who processes your data, why and to whom it was passed, to access it, to object to processing, to have it changed or destroyed, and to withdraw consent.
What is unusual about Vidlun: *almost all of this data is only ever yours to control.* It is on your phone, not with us:

bullets: withdraw consent to analysis — turn off "Entry analysis" in Me;
delete one entry — swipe it in the journal;
delete all audio — turn off "Keep recordings" in your profile;
delete everything — delete the app;
take everything with you — Backup and Readable export in your profile hand you every entry as a file (data portability, right in the app).

blocks.text: For the data held off the phone — purchases and the app check key — write to support@vidlun.app. We answer within 30 days.

*Where to complain.* In the EU, to the data protection authority of your country; in the UK, to the ICO (https://ico.org.uk); in Ukraine, to the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights (https://ombudsman.gov.ua).

blocks.heading: 6. Transfers outside Ukraine and the EEA

blocks.text: Anthropic, RevenueCat, Cloudflare and Google are in the United States. Transfers from the EU and the UK rely on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses (for the UK, with the UK Addendum to them). Transfers from Ukraine rely on your consent and on performing our contract with you (Article 29 of Ukraine's Law on Personal Data Protection).
Vidlun is meant for people aged 18 and over. If you are under 18, please do not use the app. We do not knowingly process the data of minors.

blocks.heading: 8. For US residents: consumer health data

blocks.text: Washington's My Health My Data Act and similar laws in Nevada and Connecticut require a separate account of how consumer health data is handled. For Vidlun, that is what you say about your feelings and how you are.

bullets: *What data:* the text of your entries, emotion names, mood, topics, the difficult-state flag and the monthly piece.
*Where it comes from:* only from you — what you say or type, and what the language model proposes from it.
*Why:* to provide the service you ask for: naming the emotions and topics and writing the monthly piece (section 2.1).

*Who receives it:* only processors acting under our contract and only for that purpose — Anthropic (analysis) and Cloudflare (transport). We do not sell this data and do not pass it to anyone for advertising or any other purpose.
*Your rights:* to know what data there is and who received it, to withdraw consent and to delete the data — as described in section 5. Write to support@vidlun.app; we answer within 45 days.
*Appeals.* If we decline, write to us with the subject "Appeal". We will decide within 45 days and, if we decline again, tell you how to contact your state's Attorney General.

blocks.text: If what leaves the phone changes, we will update this page and say so inside the app before the change takes effect. If a change touches what you consented to, we will ask for your consent again.
